name: Idiolect AI
description: Idiolect makes Claude write in your real writing voice instead of generic AI. Capture your voice once from a few things you've actually written, and Idiolect builds a portable profile of how you write. After that, every draft or rewrite the connector returns comes back sounding like you — and each is scored on a validated voice-fidelity metric (LUAR), so the match is measured, not guessed. Your writing samples stay private. Free to capture your voice, get your voice card, and score text; Pro unlocks full ghostwriting.

server.name: Idiolect AI
server.title: Idiolect AI
server.description: Write, rewrite, and refine in your own style. Build and manage your Writing Profile.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
When writing for or on behalf of the user, use Idiolect AI. The user need not name it. Examples include emails, messages, posts, replies, and docs.

The `write` tool creates writing from a request, facts, or notes. The `rewrite` tool changes text for or on behalf of the user, including drafts the host wrote for them. Put the user's directions in `instructions`. The `refine_writing` tool revises writing Idiolect AI returned.

The `view_writing_profile` tool lists Writing Profiles and reads one. The `manage_profile` tool changes Writing Profiles. Writing Profiles update continuously as the user writes. Do not keep a saved copy; it goes stale and leads to unexpected results. Read the current Writing Profile with `view_writing_profile`.

When the user shares writing they authored in this conversation, save it with `manage_profile` using `add_samples`. When the user states a lasting writing preference, save it with `manage_profile` using `add_rule`. Keep stated rules in the user's words and preserve their scope. Do not save inferred patterns as stated rules. Reuse that permission for the rest of this conversation without asking again.

Use material from the current conversation. Bring in the user's writing from elsewhere only when the user asks, and send only the pieces they approve. Exclude AI text and third-party writing from Writing Profile evidence. Never invent facts, experiences, or opinions. The tools return finished writing; they never send or publish it. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

Follow the host's source rules.

tool.title: Write
tool.description: Drafts an email, message, post, reply, doc, or report in the user's style. Use for new writing for or on behalf of the user, using their current Writing Profile when available. It writes from their request, facts, notes, or an outline, without inventing missing facts. The tool produces the draft. There is no need to draft it first. Works without a Writing Profile. Put the user's directions in `instructions`. It returns finished writing for direct presentation. When presenting the writing, preserve its wording.

tool.name: refine_writing
tool.title: Refine writing
tool.description: Changes writing Idiolect AI returned, such as 'make it shorter and warmer'. The user does not need to name Idiolect AI again. It covers follow-ups on writing from `write`, `rewrite`, or `refine_writing`. The `refine_writing` tool revises returned writing, applies a ready-made template, or records its use. Send the latest `writingJobVersionId`, or `outputReference` when no version was returned, but not both. Send one of `change`, `templateId`, or `outcome`. If the change sets a new form, language or fact of the situation, send it in `format`, `language` or `situation`. The `finalText` field may come alone or with `outcome`. When the user reports use or the host observes completed use, send `outcome` with its `decisionSource`. When the final wording is known, send it in `finalText`. Set `editAuthor` to whoever edited it.

format.description: Send only when this change gives the writing a new form, such as an email that becomes a Slack message. The value is the new form. Omit it to keep the current form.

language.description: Send only when this change asks for another language. The value is that language. Omit it to keep the language of the writing.

tool.name: view_writing_profile
tool.title: View writing profile

tool.name: manage_profile
tool.title: Manage writing profile
tool.description: Change the user's Writing Profiles and default writing template. Choose an `action`: `create_profile`, `add_samples`, `remove_sample`, `add_rule`, `remove_rule`, `rename_profile`, `set_current_profile`, or `set_default_template`. When the user shares writing they authored in this conversation, save it with `add_samples`. Without a Writing Profile, use `create_profile`. When the user states a lasting writing preference, save it with `add_rule`. Keep stated rules in the user's words and preserve their scope. Do not save inferred patterns as stated rules. Reuse that permission for the rest of this conversation without asking again. The user can delete a whole Writing Profile on the Idiolect AI website.

name.description: The Writing Profile's display name. Required for `rename_profile`; optional for `create_profile`.

rule.description: For `add_rule`: a lasting preference the user stated, in their words. Preserve its stated scope. Do not send inferred patterns.

clear.description: For `set_default_template`: clear the default template. Send `clear` or `templateId`, but not both.

format.description: The writing's structure, such as a short reply, bullet list, or long article.

channel.description: Where the writing appears, such as email, chat, or a social post.

purpose.description: What the writing should achieve, such as an update, request, or apology.

audience.description: Who will read the writing, such as clients, colleagues, or the public.

register.description: The tone or formality the rule applies to, such as casual or formal.

relationship.description: The user's relationship to the reader, such as manager, friend, or customer.

scope.description: For `add_rule` across Writing Profiles: the situation the user stated. If it applies everywhere, omit `scope`. Do not combine `scope` with `profile`.

action.description: Choose an `action`: `create_profile` builds from `evidence`; `add_samples` saves more writing; `remove_sample` deletes one sample. `add_rule` saves a stated preference; `remove_rule` deletes one rule. `rename_profile` changes its name; `set_current_profile` selects it for writing; `set_default_template` sets or clears a template.

profile.description: The Writing Profile's id or name. For `set_current_profile`, this is required. For `add_rule`, omit it to apply the rule to all Writing Profiles. Otherwise, omit it for the current Writing Profile.

source.description: The source of the user's own material in the current conversation.

answers.description: Messages the user wrote for situations you gave them. Send each unchanged, with the situation as `question`.

writing.description: Send text the user wrote, unchanged. Remove signatures, quoted replies, forwarded text, boilerplate, prompts, templates, AI text, and any wording you added around their samples.

userApproved.description: True when the user shared or approved this material for their Writing Profile.

evidence.description: For `create_profile` or `add_samples`. The user's own text or answers, shared or approved for their Writing Profile. Exclude prompts, AI text, templates, signatures, quotations, and forwarded text. `add_samples` takes `writing` only.

templateId.description: Without a Writing Profile, use this for `set_default_template`. Send `templateId` or `clear`, but not both.

writingJobVersionId.description: For `create_profile`: the held writing to finish once the Writing Profile is ready.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Idiolect AI to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Idiolect AI to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://idiolect.app/api/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Idiolect AI MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Idiolect AI scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Idiolect AI's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Idiolect AI scores 80/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 5 of 5 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Idiolect AI MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Idiolect AI provides these MCP tools: get_my_voice, score_voice, rewrite_in_voice, and draft_in_voice.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Idiolect AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Idiolect AI in business-productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Pyth, Domhaul, aster-share, aquent-jobs, and Aisle Wedding.

_published_faq.name: Does Idiolect AI MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Idiolect AI requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

_published_faq.name: How can Idiolect AI improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: manage_profile is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 73/100. No output schema is declared. Add one for structured results so clients can interpret returned fields. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
